description:
FILED s470bm (Opus, 2026-09-05) by the Part B item B4 census (#1172).
PRE-EXISTING.  A CLARITY defect in the IR, not a wrong answer.

THE FINDING.  The emitted CL uses a bare quoted CL symbol (`'name`) for three
things that have nothing to do with each other, and the token carries no mark
saying which:

  (a) an OPERATOR SELECTOR the runtime dispatches on —
      `(p-chain-cmp (p-aref-deref $_ 0) '> (p-aref-deref $_ 1) '>= …)`
      (perl-tests/cmpchain.t; `'<` `'<=` `'>` `'>=` `'==` `'!=`)
  (b) a HOST TYPE DESIGNATOR — `(concatenate 'string …)`, 25 occurrences in
      perl-tests/tr.t, which is CL's own vocabulary (that half is #1175)
  (c) a PROGRAM NAME — a perl loop LABEL or a bareword FILEHANDLE:
      `(catch (pcl::%pcl-loop-tag "LAST" 'start) …)`  (perl-tests/tr.t:993)
      `(p-readline 'undef)`                            (readline.t:494)
      `(p-open of "harness")`                          (flip.t:118 — `'of`)
      `'label1` `'last_113684` `'y` `'try`

A backend reading the IR must know, per CALL SITE, which of the three it is
holding.  That is exactly the kind of knowledge the IR is supposed to remove
(the OO dispatch already made the same move: ir-spec §7.3 says method names
are STRINGS, not symbols).

WHY IT COSTS SOMETHING.  A text-parsing consumer cannot classify `'start`
without knowing that `%p-loop-tag`'s second argument is a label; it cannot
classify `'>` without a table of `p-chain-cmp`'s selector set; and it cannot
tell either from `'string`, which is a host type it must not translate as
data.  The census tool has the same problem and solves it by hand — see
`@IDENT_SHAPE` and the `quoted:` bucket in tools/ir-host-leak.pl.

THE FIX DIRECTION, in the IR's own idiom:
  (a) a selector becomes a KEYWORD (`:gt`) or the runtime op name it already
      has (`p->`), which is self-describing and already in the inventory;
  (c) a label/filehandle NAME becomes a STRING, as method names are — the
      runtime already stores bareword handles by NAME (ir-spec §7.5), so the
      string is what it looks up anyway;
  (b) is #1175's job (route the emission through a `p-*` op).

Doing (a) and (c) leaves `'` in the emitted file meaning ONE thing.

BAR when taken: `tools/ir-host-leak.pl --unclassified` shows no `quoted:` rows
outside #1175's set; corpus-diff explains every diff (this IS an emission
change — bump the generation and regenerate the artifacts); the gate; the full
sweep, because the runtime side of every changed call must be changed with it;
`Pl/t/ir-host-leak-01.t`'s `chaincmp` row updated.

=== PARTLY DONE (s470bo): meaning (b) is GONE; (a) and (c) stay open ===

THE FINDING IS NOW TWO THINGS, NOT THREE.  Meaning (b), the host TYPE
designator `'string`, disappeared with #1175's family 3: a `\x{â¦}` escape and
a `tr///` range are one `(p-literal-string "piece" 55296 â¦)` call, so
`(concatenate 'string â¦)` â and the quoted `'string` inside it â is no longer
emitted anywhere.  Measured: the leak census's `quoted:string` row (25
occurrences in perl-tests/tr.t) is gone, and `Pl/t/ir-host-leak-01.t`'s
`wideescape` fixture leaks the empty set.

Family 4 also removed ONE instance of meaning (c): the `__DATA__` handle's
registration wrote the quoted handle NAME `'DATA` out, and
`p-install-data-handle` keeps it inside the runtime.

WHAT IS LEFT, and why it was not taken here:

(a) THE OPERATOR SELECTORS â `p-chain-cmp`'s `'<` `'<=` `'>` `'>=` `'==` `'!='`
    (perl-tests/cmpchain.t).  The op takes them as data and dispatches on
    them, so changing the emission means changing `p-chain-cmp`'s dispatch in
    the same commit: a keyword (`:gt`) or the runtime op name it already has
    (`p->`).  Small, but it is a RUNTIME semantic change and wants its own
    sweep leg (a `cl/**` change is invisible to corpus-diff).

(c) THE PROGRAM NAMES â a perl loop LABEL (`%pcl-loop-tag`'s second argument;
    `'start` `'label1` `'last_113684` in loopctl.t and tr.t) and a bareword
    FILEHANDLE (`(p-readline 'undef)`, `(p-open of "harness")`).  These are
    the bigger half: the bareword-handle representation is a quoted SYMBOL at
    every handle site in the runtime (`*p-filehandles*` is keyed `:test 'eq`
    on symbols), so making them STRINGS as method names are (ir-spec Â§7.3) is
    a change to the handle model â `%p-install-fh`, `%p-fh-arg`,
    `p-defined-fh`, the dup/pipe paths and the `_` stat-cache handle.  That is
    a NEW MECHANISM by the brief's own rule, so it stops here with the
    measurement rather than being half-done.

MEASUREMENT for whoever takes it: `tools/ir-host-leak.pl --unclassified` over
the 111 perl-tests files reports, after s470bo, `quoted:` rows only for
(a) â `<` `<=` `>` `>=` `==` `!=`, 26 occurrences in ONE file â and (c) â
`label1` `label2` `label3` `last_113684` `next_113684` `redo_113684` `start`
`of` `try` `undef` `y`, 22 occurrences in four files.  So (a) is one file's
worth of dispatch and (c) is the handle model; the split is clean.
subject: A QUOTED SYMBOL in the IR is three unrelated things - an operator selector, a host TYPE designator, and a perl label/filehandle NAME - and a consumer cannot tell them apart
